title: Add VPC control plane provisioning: multi-AZ subnets, interface endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: add a first-class Terraform module and companion Helm/installer changes to fully provision the VPC control plane for Private deployments across multiple AZs. This PR codifies: 1) multi-AZ subnets and route tables for the control plane, 2) interface and gateway endpoints for required AWS services (S3, ECR, Systems Manager), 3) security group templates and least-privilege ingress/egress between control-plane and data-plane subnets, 4) cross-account VPC peering and route propagation guidance, and 5) automated Route53 private hosted zone creation and conditional DNS peering records. The change set is intended to make Private control plane bootstrap repeatable and auditable for both VPC-based private and air-gapped deployments. Checklist: - [x] Terraform module: control-plane/vpc (subnets, nat, route tables, tags) - [x] Terraform module: control-plane/endpoints (interface endpoints, gateway endpoints) - [x] Security: control-plane SG templates and IAM policy examples - [x] Cross-account peering module + examples (account IDs redacted) - [x] Route53 private hosted zone + peering records automation - [x] Helm: installer values + templates to accept new network outputs - [x] Upgrade/rollback notes and test plan included - [x] E2E smoke run in staging and manual multi-AZ deploy validated Summary of changes: - New Terraform modules under redwood-private-installer/terraform/modules/control-plane/{vpc,endpoints,peering,dns,sg} - Updated example stacks under redwood-private-installer/terraform/examples/multi-az-control-plane - Helm chart changes to redwood-helm-charts/private-control-plane to accept network outputs and create k8s EndpointSlices for service discovery - Installer CLI changes to map Terraform outputs to Helm values during install/upgrade - Documentation updates to redwood-docs/private/install/vpc-control-plane.md Testing & validation: - CI: terraform fmt/validate, terratested plan runs for examples (passed), helm lint (passed), chart-testing (passed) - Manual: deployed control plane into staging account across 3 AZs, validated cross-AZ failover, confirmed KV cache connectivity between control-plane pods and data-plane nodes, validated Route53 resolution across peered VPCs - Smoke tests: API health, token auth, basic inference path (successful) Rollback strategy: - Helm rollout with previous chart artifact (helm rollback) and Terraform destroy/apply targeted to revert peering/resources created by example stacks - Provided a script examples/rollback/rollback-control-plane.sh and explicit instructions in docs for forced tear-down in case of partial failure Security review: limited IAM changes included as examples only; no production credentials are checked in. Follow-ups: - Add automated acceptance tests to perf-canary for multi-AZ control plane latencies (ENG-3497) - Add IAM bootstrap automation for peering cross-account role assumption (separate PR) Related: linear tickets ENG-3421, ENG-3497. See internal runbook link: https://linear.app/redwood/board/ENG/issue/ENG-3421 (internal) for rollout schedule.

release_notes: Adds Terraform modules and Helm mappings to provision and manage Private control plane network topology (multi-AZ subnets, endpoints, SGs, peering, Route53). Includes upgrade/rollback guidance and examples.
notes_for_operators: When deploying to production accounts, replace example account IDs, run terratest in a purpose-built CI worker with appropriate IAM, and ensure Route53 peering approvals are completed. Use provided rollback script for partial failures.
